solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Not very great shopping centre is in outskirts of Slough

indicators.note: the shopping centre and 'is' sit in the outer letters
outskirts are the edges of a town, so take only the first and last letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of SLOUGH
a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: A modest shopping mall on the edge of Slough, a town west of London.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'is' is not a link word here; it goes into the box alongside MALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Smallish means fairly small, so not very great.

clue.text: Snake enters dilapidated housing quietly

indicators.note: a dilapidated building has fallen apart, so rearrange the letters
the rearranged letters hold P inside them

explanation.surface: A snake slithers into a derelict house without a sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enters' reads as the snake's verb, but it is the word to be rearranged, and 'quietly' is the musical p that goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: serpent is the older, more literary word for a snake, as in the serpent in Eden.

clue.text: Delight American showed in games boundlessly

indicators.note: US is shown into the middle of the other letters
without its bounds, GAMES loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: GAMES without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An American delights in showing off at the games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' wants to be the single letter A; here it is the two-letter abbreviation, sitting inside the trimmed game word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to give pleasure, as a good joke does its listener.

clue.text: Officers fib, you said, before number of soldiers

indicators.note: 'you' spoken sounds like the letter U
LIE and U come before the rest

blocks.note: the letter U is pronounced like 'you'
soldier ants: 'soldiers' is a crossword stand-in for ants

explanation.surface: Officers tell lies about how many troops they have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number of soldiers' reads as a troop count; it splits into a number and an insect, since soldiers are a caste of ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: lieutenant is one rank of commissioned officer, in army and navy alike.

clue.text: I must replace area of tray made of metal

indicators.note: I takes the place of the A

blocks.note: a salver is a serving tray
a = area; this A comes out
goes in where the A was

explanation.surface: An instruction to swap part of a metal tray.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an adjective phrase, as in a silver spoon.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective sense: a silver cup or spoon is one made of that precious metal.

clue.text: Develop good argument

blocks.note: a row (rhymes with 'cow') is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A healthy argument helps you grow as a person.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a row, said to rhyme with 'now', is a noisy argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a child or a business can be said to develop or to grow.

clue.text: Concerned about a child’s motives

blocks.note: a son is a child; the apostrophe is ignored

explanation.surface: Worrying about why a child behaves as they do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concerned about' looks like worry but is just RE, as in the heading of a memo.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what drove someone to act are the motives behind it.

clue.text: Unite opposing sides in graduate club

indicators.note: the two sides of GRADUATE, its first and last letters

blocks.note: to wed is to unite in marriage
first and last letters of GRADUATE

explanation.surface: Rival factions come together in an alumni society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Graduate club' reads as a society; the club is a golf club, the wedge.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedge is a golf club for short lofted shots.

clue.text: Run no further, regularly missing path

indicators.note: every other letter goes missing, leaving the even ones

blocks.note: r = run, as in cricket scores
the even letters of NO FURTHER: nO fUrThEr

explanation.surface: A runner who can go no further, having lost the path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run no further' reads as a runner giving up, but it is R plus a letter pick.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the way you take from one place to another is your path.

clue.text: Tight-fitting garment was first donned by old sailor

indicators.note: a garment donned is worn around you, so LED wraps the rest

blocks.note: to have led is to have been first

explanation.surface: An old sailor was the first to squeeze into a tight garment.
explanation.walkthrough: The garment in the surface is the answer itself; the wordplay reads LE(O TAR)D.
explanation.definitionFit: A leotard is a close-fitting one-piece garment worn by dancers and gymnasts.

clue.text: Six deliveries a vendor arranged repeatedly

indicators.note: the letters of A VENDOR are put in a new order

blocks.note: in cricket an over is six balls bowled

explanation.surface: A vendor sets up the same six deliveries again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' suggests parcels, but these are cricket balls: an over is six balls bowled by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: doing something time after time, again and again.

clue.text: Finally restore the ancient organ

indicators.note: take the final letter of RESTORE

blocks.note: ye is an old spelling of 'the', as in Ye Olde Shoppe

explanation.surface: An instruction to restore an ancient organ, as in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient organ' paints a church instrument; the organ is the eye, and 'the ancient' is YE.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: of the body's sense organs, this is the one for sight.

clue.text: So entertained by act here for evening

indicators.note: the answer is held within the words that follow

blocks.note: hidden in acT HERE FOR Evening

explanation.surface: A performance is put on here for the evening's entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre picture hides the answer across four words.
explanation.definitionFit: Therefore and so both mean for that reason.

clue.text: Cheers monarch is receiving

blocks.note: ta is British informal for thanks, like 'cheers'

explanation.surface: A monarch is being toasted as the crowd cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' suggests a toast, but in British usage both 'cheers' and 'ta' mean thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking and receiving both mean accepting what is given.

clue.text: Equipment that man installed in empty common room

indicators.note: HE is fitted inside the other letters
emptied of its middle, COMMON keeps only C and N

explanation.surface: A man fits equipment in an unoccupied common room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common room' looks like one phrase and a definition, but only 'room' defines; 'common' is emptied to CN.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the room of a house where food is cooked.

clue.text: Had success in test — that’s given

blocks.note: first sense: got through an exam
second sense: handed over, as with the salt at table

explanation.surface: Passing the test is taken for granted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's given' reads as 'that's a certainty'; it is the second meaning, handed over.
explanation.definitionFit: Passed means both succeeded in a test and handed to someone.

clue.text: Cursorily read old papers in retirement, consuming some beer

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so O and ID are turned round
the turned letters take PINT inside them

blocks.note: a pint is a measure of beer

explanation.surface: A retired person leafs through old papers over a beer.
explanation.walkthrough: The retiree in the surface is a reversal: retiring goes back, so the old papers are read backwards before the beer goes inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: To dip into a book is to read bits of it casually.

clue.text: Equilibrium not entirely lost as I swerved

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used

blocks.note: hidden in loST AS I Swerved

explanation.surface: A driver who swerved nearly lost their balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swerved' hints at an anagram, but the answer runs straight through the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of balance where nothing changes.

clue.text: Noted date suspect set off

indicators.note: suspect means unreliable, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: A recorded date for when a suspect left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' looks like a noun, a person under suspicion; here it is an adjective telling you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a bomb that has been triggered to explode has been set off.

clue.text: Stink after gutting fish all around harbourside

indicators.note: a gutted STINK loses its insides, leaving S and K
the whole string is turned around

explanation.surface: Gutting fish leaves a stench all around the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' is not an order word here: 'after gutting' means once the smell word is gutted. Its remains go first, the fish second, and the whole lot is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Docks are the part of a port along the harbourside.

clue.text: Strike old boy back with power

indicators.note: going back means travelling in reverse, so the old boy's letters are read the other way

blocks.note: OB = old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: Hitting an old boy back hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old boy' is British for a former pupil of a school, shortened to OB.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: a bop is a light blow, so to deliver one is to strike.

clue.text: Upset, cry about conclusions of you being fake

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the letters upside down, so read them backwards
SOB goes around the other letters
the last letters of YOU and BEING

blocks.note: last letters of YOU and BEING

explanation.surface: Someone upset and in tears about being called a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: S(UG)OB is built first and then the whole thing is turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a bogus doctor or a bogus claim is a fake one.

clue.text: I’m surprised, overwhelmed by expenditure for presenting duo

definitions.note: 'duo' names the pair; CO-HOSTS names its members

indicators.note: OH is swamped by, and so inside, COSTS

explanation.surface: A pair of TV presenters shocked at how much they have spent.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation lands just after the first letter of the spending word, splitting it.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people who present a show together are its co-hosts.

clue.text: One dodging certain fare, say, aboard transport

indicators.note: EG is on board, inside, the vehicle

blocks.note: a van is a means of transport

explanation.surface: A fare dodger riding a bus or train without paying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' suggests a ticket price; it is food, and a vegan dodges meat and dairy.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegan avoids certain food, namely animal products.

clue.text: Go astray by end of corporate function

indicators.note: take the last letter of CORPORATE

blocks.note: to sin is to go morally astray

explanation.surface: Misbehaving at the office party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporate function' paints an office event; the function is the trigonometric one.
explanation.definitionFit: A mathematical sense: one of the trigonometric functions, alongside cosine and tangent.

clue.text: Cook reposes with second coffee

indicators.note: to cook the books is to rework them, so rearrange the letters

blocks.note: s = second, added to the fodder

explanation.surface: A cook relaxing with a quick coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' reads as a person resting; it is the verb telling you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a strong black coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.
